messages.content: 你能幫我找到紐約有閱讀室和小說區的公共圖書館，然後在洛杉磯有Wi-Fi和有兒童區的公共圖書館，最後在芝加哥有咖啡廳和閱讀室的公共圖書館嗎？

function.name: public_library_find_nearby
function.description: Locate nearby public libraries based on specific criteria like English fiction availability and Wi-Fi. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The city and state, e.g. Boston, MA

facilities.description: Facilities and sections in public library.

The user wants to find libraries in three cities with certain facilities. We need to call the function multiple times. The function signature: public_library_find_nearby takes location string and facilities which can be one of the enumerated strings? Wait facilities param type: "Wi-Fi" | "Reading Room" | "Fiction" | "Children Section" | "Cafe"[].

It seems facilities expects a single value or an array? The type says "Wi-Fi" | "Reading Room" | "Fiction" | "Children Section" | "Cafe"[]. That means it can be one of those strings or an array of "Cafe"? Actually "Cafe"[] indicates array of Cafe? But maybe they want to pass array of facilities? The example: "Facilities and sections in public library." So we might pass an array of strings like ["Reading Room", "Fiction"] etc. But the type says union of string or array of "Cafe". Might be mis-specified. Let's assume we can pass array of strings.

We need to call function thrice:

1. location: "New York, NY" (or "New York, NY") facilities: ["Reading Room", "Fiction"]
2. location: "Los Angeles, CA" facilities: ["Wi-Fi", "Children Section"]
3. location: "Chicago, IL" facilities: ["Cafe", "Reading Room"]

We need to output the results. We'll call function each time. Use the function tool.
